skill.name: codex
skill.description: Use this skill to run Codex CLI from Claude Code for code review, refactoring, editing, and session resume workflows.
skill.summary: Run Codex CLI tasks and resume Codex sessions from Claude Code.
skill.author: softaworks

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are Markdown documentation or normal installation paths, but the skill does enable real external Codex execution. The main risks are full-auto broad-access modes, shell prompt piping during resume, and default stderr suppression.

remediation.issue: High-impact Codex execution modes are documented for use.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before workspace-write, full-auto, danger-full-access, network access, or skip-git-repo-check modes.

remediation.issue: Resume examples pipe prompt text through echo into a shell command.
remediation.suggestion: Pass prompts through safe stdin handling without shell interpolation, or clearly require robust shell escaping.

remediation.issue: stderr is suppressed by default for Codex commands.
remediation.suggestion: Show stderr for failures and safety warnings, or capture it separately for review instead of discarding it.

remediation.issue: Installation instructions use a temporary clone copied into a hidden skills directory.
remediation.suggestion: Document the exact install destination and advise users to inspect the skill before copying it into Claude settings.

semantic_findings.title: High-Impact Autonomous Codex Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill enables Codex runs with full-auto and danger-full-access for broad filesystem or network access. User approval is required, but the capability is high impact.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Multiple instructions explicitly mention sandbox selection, full-auto, and danger-full-access. The text includes a permission gate, so intent appears operational rather than malicious.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Shell Prompt Piping Pattern
semantic_findings.description: The resume workflow shows user prompt text being piped through echo into a shell command. Without careful escaping, prompt text could alter shell behavior.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples use shell echo with placeholder prompt text. The risk depends on implementation, but agents may interpolate untrusted user prompts directly.

semantic_findings.title: Default Suppression Of Codex Diagnostics
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells agents to hide stderr from Codex commands by default. This can conceal warnings, failures, or safety-relevant diagnostic output from review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation repeatedly states that stderr is redirected to /dev/null. It gives a benign rationale, but diagnostics can contain important warnings.

content.value_statement: Claude Code users often need deeper code analysis or automated edits from Codex. This skill gives Claude a structured way to launch Codex, choose safe execution settings, and summarize results.
actual_capabilities: Runs Codex CLI tasks with selected model and reasoning effort settings.
Resumes the most recent Codex session when the user asks to continue.
Chooses sandbox modes for read-only review, local edits, or broader access.
Suppresses stderr by default unless the user requests debugging output.
Summarizes Codex output and asks for next-step confirmation.
Documents model options and recommended effort levels for coding tasks.
limitations: Requires Codex CLI version 0.57.0 or later on the local PATH.
Requires configured Codex credentials before commands can run.
High-impact modes can edit files or allow broad system access.
Model names, pricing, and benchmark claims may change over time.

use_cases.title: Repository Review
use_cases.description: Ask Codex to inspect a repository and return prioritized engineering improvements.

use_cases.title: Guided Refactoring
use_cases.description: Use Codex to plan or apply refactors while Claude coordinates review and follow-up.

use_cases.title: Resume Agent Work
use_cases.description: Continue a previous Codex session without rebuilding the full task context.

prompt_templates.title: Review This Repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Codex to review this repository in read-only mode. Summarize the top issues and suggest practical next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan A Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Codex with high reasoning effort to plan a refactor for this module. Do not edit files yet.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Focused Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Codex to implement the approved change in workspace-write mode. Show the changed files and any tests run.

prompt_templates.title: Resume And Verify
prompt_templates.prompt: Resume the last Codex session. Ask it to verify the previous changes and identify any remaining risks.

output_examples.input: Use Codex to analyze this Claude Code skill repository.
output_examples.output: A concise review with security notes, implementation risks, and recommended follow-up actions.

output_examples.input: Resume the last Codex session and continue the refactor review.
output_examples.output: A continuation summary that preserves the prior session context and lists next decisions.

output_examples.input: Use Codex to apply the approved bug fix.
output_examples.output: A change summary with affected files, verification results, and any unresolved concerns.

best_practices: Start in read-only mode for analysis before allowing edits.
Ask for explicit approval before using full-auto or danger-full-access modes.
Review Codex output and local diffs before accepting changes.
anti_patterns: Do not run broad-access commands for simple review tasks.
Do not hide stderr when debugging failures or safety warnings.
Do not resume a session with sensitive prompts unless the user approves.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It lets Claude Code run Codex CLI tasks and resume Codex sessions for coding workflows.

faq.question: Does it require Codex CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. Codex CLI must be installed, available on PATH, and configured with valid credentials.

faq.question: Can it edit files?
faq.answer: Yes, when workspace-write or broader sandbox modes are selected for an approved task.

faq.question: Can it access the network?
faq.answer: It can when danger-full-access is selected. Users should approve that mode before use.

faq.question: Why is stderr hidden by default?
faq.answer: The skill hides stderr to reduce context size, but debugging and warnings may need stderr output.

faq.question: Is this safe for private repositories?
faq.answer: Use caution. Codex may process repository content, prompts, and command output through configured Codex services.
